newsitem.title: HUNGARY: HUNGARY GOVT SAYS READY TO TALK WITH ANGRY FARMERS.
newsitem.headline: HUNGARY GOVT SAYS READY TO TALK WITH ANGRY FARMERS.

text.p: The Hungarian government said on Thursday it was ready for talks with farmers to prevent their planned three-day blockade of main roads on Monday to protest new tax regulations.

"The government hopes that those who plan the demonstration, will take into consideration the readiness which the government showed for a compromise," Prime Minister's Office Secretary of State Elemer Kiss told a news conference.

The farmers presented a petition last week to the agricultural ministry demanding that the cabinet should withdraw tax and social security measures introduced on January 1 which they say jeopardise their livelihood.

The farmers said that if the government does not meet their demands for changing 1997 tax regulations, they will set up over 25 road blocks outside key towns around Hungary, a move which will almost certainly paralyse the country's road system.
The government on Thursday approved law amendments which relieved farmers from certain tax and administrative burdens.
However, Kiss said that the government would not reinstate 1996 tax and social security contribution rules.
He added that the agricultural minister would negotiate with the farmers on behalf of the government.
